title: Practicing, his strict father and Slap Room Johnny
summary: Closing question on youth: his father made him practice clarinet, and he recalls pianist Slap Room Johnny and appreciating his father's strictness.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers

blocks.x: We have about another minute or so on here. Yeah, well. Is there anything else you can tell about when you were young to finish up your life?
Well when I was young, when I was young, when I was young.
When you had lessons, how much did you practice?

Well I had to practice, my daddy used to see that every half an hour before I go to school tomorrow I had to practice and then when I come home in the evening I had to practice before I go outside and play. Had to practice, yeah. If we didn't practice we couldn't go outside. In other words we had to practice regardless of whether you go outside or not, you had to practice. And with your clarinet?

I don't think I practiced over an hour myself. I was on the clarinet, yeah. Had to practice on the clarinet, just like I told him when John Bruce would come home or pick his daddy, play this, play this. I said I can't play that, but you're going to try to play it. My mother would tell him, don't hurt that boy, he's going to play it. I learned how to play his piano, didn't I? Yeah, he would punch you. Nothing make out of it, he'd punch you. And he was a half way of price for that too, he was called Slap Room Johnny. Oh yeah? Yeah, yeah.
Well that's right, yeah. I think I told him that. Yeah, yeah, I remember that. Yeah, yeah, yeah.

He was one of those fellas who wore the beautiful stick, such with his stick pin and his beautiful monogram, buckle, wall, very proud, yeah. Dress of all the time. He'd just come out the house and he'd play some blues and never knew what key he was in or nothing. Listen, listen at it, you listen at it. You get it and I'd have to get down, I'd better play at something. I'd better play at it. I mean, but that really helped out the whole lot. Oh yeah, you wouldn't realize. People don't know. Just like I tell people, I was a big man when I walked to my dad every time I'd see him and kiss him. Because I mean, I appreciate, he was tough. Oh, probably you had to toe the mark. But I appreciate it. I really do. Yeah, he was a tough old man.
